findings.issue: HEAD^ is accepted whenever HEAD is a tracking-artifact-only commit, but the code never verifies that the HEAD tracking commit belongs to the same phase. This violates the required rule: HEAD^ is valid only when HEAD is a same-phase tracking-artifact-only commit. I reproduced a false pass where phaseResult.phase_id is phase-1, commit_records points to HEAD^, and HEAD contains phase-result.json for phase-2; validatePhaseGate still returned ok:true.
findings.recommendation: When allowing HEAD^, inspect the tracking commit content or committed phase-result.json and verify it records the same phase_id as phaseResult.phase_id. Add a regression test where HEAD is a tracking-only commit for a different phase and the gate must fail.

resolutionSummary: Tests reported in the review package pass, and I re-ran the stated test command successfully: 4 files, 102 tests passed. One blocking correctness gap remains in the phase-gate commit validation: cross-phase tracking commits can incorrectly authorize HEAD^.

findings.description: Spec describes or requires eliminating internal contradictions between field contracts or rule statements (cluster A: schema/contract terms + cluster B: conflict/contradiction/duplicate terms). Multiple conflicting schemas for the same entity cause silent drift — schema-drift blocking.
